headline_marked: Up to 200,000 people: [[US to revoke visas of asylum seekers]]
headline: Up to 200,000 people: US to revoke visas of asylum seekers
summary: The Trump administration targets foreigners who entered on tourist or business visas but applied for asylum to stay permanently.
details: The US government plans to revoke the visas of foreigners who entered the country for tourism or business but later applied for asylum to stay permanently.
The White House suggested that up to 200,000 visas could be affected, potentially making it the largest mass visa revocation in history.
State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott stated that obtaining a visa specifically to seek asylum is considered fraud and grounds for revocation.
Since President Donald Trump returned to power in January 2025, approximately 175,000 foreigners have already had their visas revoked for various reasons, including criminal offenses.
The administration is also expanding the vetting of social media accounts for visa applicants as part of a broader drive to reduce immigration.
While some measures have been challenged in court, the administration maintains that a visa is a privilege and not a right.
caption:
Up to 200,000 visas could be revoked. The US is cracking down on those who used tourist or business visas to seek asylum.

The US government plans to revoke the visas of foreigners who entered the country for tourism or business but later applied for asylum to stay permanently.

The White House suggested that up to 200,000 visas could be affected, potentially making it the largest mass visa revocation in history.

State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott stated that obtaining a visa specifically to seek asylum is considered fraud and grounds for revocation.

Since President Donald Trump returned to power in January 2025, approximately 175,000 foreigners have already had their visas revoked for various reasons, including criminal offenses.

The administration is also expanding the vetting of social media accounts for visa applicants as part of a broader drive to reduce immigration.

While some measures have been challenged in court, the administration maintains that a visa is a privilege and not a right.

headline_marked: Rangpur: [[Four members of a teacher's family killed]], funeral rites held
headline: Rangpur: Four members of a teacher's family killed, funeral rites held
summary: Family members and locals expressed deep anger and demanded a swift investigation into the brutal killings in Machhuapara.
details: Funeral rites for the four members of a teacher's family killed in Rangpur city were performed on Tuesday, August 25.
The ceremony took place from morning until night at the victims' home and a nearby temple in Machhuapara, following Hindu rituals.
Rangpur City Corporation administrator Mahfuz Un Nabi Don and people from various professions attended the rites to pray for the souls of the deceased.
Despite the solemnity, family members and locals expressed intense anger, demanding the mystery of the brutal killings be uncovered and those responsible be brought to justice.
Administrator Mahfuz Un Nabi Don urged the public to provide any critical information to law enforcement agencies to help solve the case.
He emphasized that law enforcement needs reasonable time to uncover the true mystery of the killings and called for patience from the community.
Don also warned residents to be cautious and not allow any individual or group to misrepresent the event for political purposes.
The family and locals continue to demand a swift conclusion to the investigation and exemplary punishment for the perpetrators.
caption:
A teacher's family of four was brutally killed in Rangpur. Funeral rites were held amid deep anger and grief.

Funeral rites for the four members of a teacher's family killed in Rangpur city were performed on Tuesday, August 25.

The ceremony took place from morning until night at the victims' home and a nearby temple in Machhuapara, following Hindu rituals.

Rangpur City Corporation administrator Mahfuz Un Nabi Don and people from various professions attended the rites to pray for the souls of the deceased.

Despite the solemnity, family members and locals expressed intense anger, demanding the mystery of the brutal killings be uncovered and those responsible be brought to justice.

Administrator Mahfuz Un Nabi Don urged the public to provide any critical information to law enforcement agencies to help solve the case.

He emphasized that law enforcement needs reasonable time to uncover the true mystery of the killings and called for patience from the community.

Don also warned residents to be cautious and not allow any individual or group to misrepresent the event for political purposes.

The family and locals continue to demand a swift conclusion to the investigation and exemplary punishment for the perpetrators.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star
